channel.title: Updated · Tech
channel.description: Chips, software, security, devices and space (beyond AI)

item.title: A Microsoft 365 outage tied to Exchange Online knocks out email, Teams and Copilot for more than 12 hours
item.description: Microsoft 365 services that depend on Exchange Online failed worldwide from Thursday afternoon, and Microsoft's fixes had not brought sustained recovery more than 12 hours later. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: Apache patches a critical HTTP/2 flaw in its web server that could let attackers run code remotely
item.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 fixes a critical race condition in its HTTP/2 module that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code on servers that have HTTP/2 switched on. (Apache HTTP Server Project, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Police in nine countries seize 235 servers behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware
item.description: An Operation Endgame action coordinated by Europol took down 235 servers and 257 domains used by three malware families and found about 6.4 million stolen credentials. (BleepingComputer, The Record)

item.title: Google opens pre-orders for its first Gemini smart glasses, made with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and Samsung
item.description: Google's camera-equipped "intelligent eyewear," starting at $395, is up for pre-order ahead of a December 10 launch, with privacy limits such as a tamper-checked recording light. (Google, Ars Technica)

item.title: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays
item.description: A design for neutral-atom quantum computers that picks which qubits to operate on by moving helper atoms, letting simple global laser and microwave pulses run error-corrected computation in simulation. (Zhihao Zhang, Shuaifan Cao, Xinyang Yu et al. · Fudan University)

item.title: Attackers push rogue remote-access clients to hundreds of PCs through managed service providers' ScreenConnect panels
item.description: Attackers used cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to install rogue remote-access software on at least 288 computers at 48 organizations; ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions across about 400 partner environments. (BleepingComputer, Huntress)

item.title: Maersk confirms data theft from a legacy logistics system as a ransomware gang demands $5 million
item.description: Maersk says attackers stole data from an isolated system inherited through an acquisition; the WhiteArmor gang claims about 100GB and wants $5 million in bitcoin within 30 days. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: The EU proposes a Digital Fairness Act to ban dark patterns, rein in addictive design and limit loot boxes for minors
item.description: The European Commission's draft Digital Fairness Act would ban manipulative "dark patterns," let users switch off addictive features, curb pay-to-win games for minors and allow fines of up to 6% of global turnover. (The Verge, Engadget)

item.title: IBM's quantum roadmap swaps nine linked chips for two larger ones, targeting about 1,040 qubits in 2027
item.description: At its developer conference, IBM said its current Nighthawk r2 chip runs circuits of over 7,500 operations, and planned a 520-qubit Nighthawk r3 for 2027, with two chips linked into a roughly 1,040-qubit system. (IBM Quantum, Ars Technica)

item.title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
item.description: PRISM, a transformer-based decoder for photonic quantum computers, matches slower integer-programming decoders on accuracy and runs on an AMD FPGA with 6.59-microsecond latency. (Daniel Barter, Jacob C. Bridgeman, Chris Dawson et al.)

item.title: France formally blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for the cyberattacks that heated supermarket freezers
item.description: France says an Iranian Revolutionary Guards cyber unit sabotaged refrigeration controllers at more than 700 grocery stores, causing at least 15 fires, and plans to push for EU sanctions. (The Register, TechCrunch)

item.title: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday fixes over 1,000 flaws, including an Outlook bug already used to steal logins
item.description: Microsoft's monthly updates fix between 1,093 and 1,235 vulnerabilities depending on how they are counted, including an exploited Outlook spoofing flaw, alongside patches from Apple, Google, Mozilla and Adobe. (BleepingComputer, Krebs on Security)

item.title: N-able takes its N-central remote-management cloud offline after a researcher publishes 30-plus unpatched flaws
item.description: After a researcher released working exploits for more than 30 alleged flaws without warning, N-able shut down hosted N-central worldwide and told on-premises customers to switch their servers off. (BleepingComputer, TechCrunch)

item.title: Mitsui Chemicals agrees to buy photoresist maker JSR for $11.6 billion
item.description: Mitsui Chemicals will pay 1.84 trillion yen for JSR, a leading maker of the light-sensitive coatings used to print chip circuits, in the largest deal ever in Japan's chemicals sector. (Reuters via The Star, WebProNews)

item.title: SFU-Sim: Bit-Exact Reverse Engineering of NVIDIA MUFU and Validation of PTX Paths
item.description: SFU-Sim reverse-engineers how Nvidia GPUs compute sine, cosine and other special functions, and its model matches real hardware bit for bit on every input across three GPU generations. (Haozhi Xie, Tao Su · Sun Yat-sen University)

item.title: Attackers are exploiting the "SSHole" OpenSSH flaw on Alpine-style Linux servers days after the fix
item.description: Several security firms report real attacks on the OpenSSH and musl flaw CVE-2026-123158, which can give logins to passwordless accounts; OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes it. (Ars Technica, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Vanderbilt University tells campus to shut down devices as the new BYOD ransomware gang claims an attack
item.description: Vanderbilt confirmed an active cyber incident and asked everyone to power off devices; a ransomware group called BYOD claims it stole data on over a million people. (The Record, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Congress summons Nvidia's CEO over a reported Chinese spy operation, and Nvidia's board opens an investigation
item.description: House committee chairs asked Jensen Huang to brief them on November 18 about reported Chinese spying aimed at him; on Sunday Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation. (Ars Technica, TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: SonicWall patches a firewall VPN flaw that can sidestep SAML multi-factor login and is already exploited
item.description: SonicWall fixed seven SonicOS flaws, including CVE-2026-19868, which can bypass SAML-enforced MFA on SSL-VPN logins and was added to CISA's catalog of exploited bugs. (SonicWall advisory (as quoted by SecurityWeek), BleepingComputer, Help Net Security)

item.title: Chainalysis says hackers obtained credentials and live tokens for all of its users
item.description: Chainalysis, whose tools trace cryptocurrency flows, now says names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for every user were exposed, widening an incident first described as limited. (BleepingComputer, Ars Technica)

item.title: DigiCert says a 16-month exposure of an internal system let an outsider read customer identity documents
item.description: DigiCert says a server migration left an internal archive reachable from the internet from February 2025, and an unauthorized account read some customer records in June and July 2026. (The Register, The Record)

item.title: Fox completes its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, five months after announcing it
item.description: Fox closed its $22 billion purchase of Roku, which reaches more than 100 million households, far earlier than the first-half-2027 completion the companies had projected. (TechCrunch, Engadget)

item.title: AST SpaceMobile plans its own medium-lift rocket, backed by a $1.3 billion Firefly engine deal
item.description: The direct-to-phone satellite company says it will build Blacklift, a 20-ton-class rocket, and has committed $1.3 billion to Firefly for engines, a license and engineering support. (Ars Technica, Firefly Aerospace newsroom (headline))

item.title: FaultScope: A software package for fast error attribution in quantum error correction
item.description: FaultScope is an open-source simulator that estimates how much each noisy component contributes to logical errors in quantum error correction, at under 1% extra runtime in tests. (Yuguo Shao, Zhenyu Chen, Ningfeng Wang et al. · Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, Tsinghua University; Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications; Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University)

item.title: OpenSSH patch fixes "*sshole", a ten-year-old login bypass on musl-based Linux systems
item.description: OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes a flaw, present since 2016, that lets an oversized password log in to accounts meant to refuse passwords on musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: Blue Origin pushes the next New Glenn launch into January 2027 after May launchpad explosion
item.description: Blue Origin's CEO told staff the next New Glenn flight is now targeted for January 2027, after earlier hopes of launching before the end of this year. (Engadget, The Verge)

item.title: FAA begins replacing floppy-disk-based air traffic displays with a digital system at more than 400 facilities
item.description: The FAA says it will replace 1980s display systems that run on floppy disks with the digital E-IDS platform, targeting 435 sites by the end of 2028. (Engadget, FAA)

item.title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware
item.description: Callix, a tool that judges whether access checks are strong enough for a sensitive operation, found 819 vulnerable paths in pre-installed apps from ten Android vendors. (Haotian Deng, Meng Hao, Hanxiao Chen et al. · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China)

item.title: Second wave of attacks on refrigeration controllers hits supermarkets across Europe
item.description: Remote tampering with refrigeration controllers raised temperatures in more than 115 stores in six European countries on November 2, and also reached a French blood-service supplier, following a larger French wave in October. (Al Jazeera, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Zyxel patches a switch flaw that was exploited on nearly 1,000 devices after being mistaken for an older bug
item.description: Zyxel fixed CVE-2026-107441 in ten GS1900 switch models after attackers used it to compromise 996 devices; the bug had been misattributed to an earlier, already-patched flaw. (BleepingComputer, Help Net Security)

item.title: Suspected Russian hackers use patched iPhone and Android flaws in watering-hole attacks
item.description: Sekoia says a group it links to Russia's foreign intelligence service used websites to profile visitors and attack phones that had not installed existing security updates. (Ars Technica, Sekoia blog)

item.title: DreamHost confirms a two-month breach of its File Manager exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
item.description: Web host DreamHost says an attacker exploited a flaw in its File Manager from August to October 23, stealing FTP/SFTP credentials and some webmail session data. (BleepingComputer, TechCrunch)

item.title: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal
item.description: Chip designer Marvell will acquire optical component maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt, expected to close in the first half of 2028. (TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE)

item.title: Google and partners dismantle XCPE botnet built into 1.3 million Android TV boxes
item.description: Google's Threat Intelligence Group and partners disrupted XCPE, a backdoor that a Chinese manufacturer shipped in more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes to rent out owners' internet connections. (Krebs on Security, Ars Technica, The Register)

item.title: Binance says a fake job interview started its $6.3 billion theft
item.description: Binance's incident report says a multi-stage attack beginning with a fake recruiter and malware led to the October 29 theft of about $6.34 billion, which the FBI attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor group. (BleepingComputer, The Register, WIRED)

item.title: Apple warns memory costs are unprecedented as they squeeze margins and Mac supply
item.description: On its earnings call, Apple said memory pricing is unprecedented, forecast a December-quarter gross margin of 45 to 46 percent and expects Mac and iPad supply constraints. (TechCrunch, 9to5Mac, The Register)
